PullRequest.Title: Polish HydraFusion model picker descriptions
PullRequest.Body:
HydraFusion should remain concise beside the Auto tiers while still explaining its routing behavior and linking to more context.

## Changes
- keep the legacy picker description unchanged and add an inline Learn more link
- use concise row text and a richer reusable flyout in the tabbed picker
- expose flyout controls through shared hover content instead of DOM selector queries
- document and test keyboard access to the Learn more link

Scenarios.Scenario: Open the tabbed model picker in Auto mode with HydraFusion available
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Build provider sections and action-list descriptors, render visible rows, and synchronously measure/layout the existing action list. The new HydraFusion flyout DOM is not constructed on this path because hover.content is a function.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of configured language models controls existing picker list construction; this diff adds one HydraFusion descriptor and one closure, independent of model count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single UI-thread list construction and layout; no parallel work or queueing is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The flyout starts cold and unconstructed. Its descriptor-local content is reused while live and rebuilt after explicit disposal or list replacement; no cross-popup cache or negative-cache behavior is involved.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: _buildAutoModeItems creates only localized strings and a lazy content callback; getModelHoverContent is reached only when the panel opens.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact list layout duration depends on model count and platform, but the incremental work is constant and excludes markdown/DOM flyout construction.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the PR keeps the added markdown and controls off picker-open critical path and adds constant descriptor work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open and navigate the HydraFusion description flyout by pointer or keyboard
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The first panel open synchronously calls getModelHoverContent, renders one short MarkdownString and one anchor, attaches it to the existing action-list submenu panel, and performs the action-list's normal panel geometry/layout. This must finish before the flyout is visible and focus can enter Learn more.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One HydraFusion row and one short localized paragraph per panel open; work does not scale with the total model collection or history.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serialized on the UI thread. The action-list uses one current submenu panel, so repeated focus changes replace rather than concurrently fan out panels.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A warm open reuses the descriptor-local hoverContent. When a replacement preservation probe rejects newly built content, disposeContent releases it; popup/widget disposal releases the active DisposableStore. There is no unbounded key set.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed callback, shared renderer, action-list show path, disposal hook, and tabbable element list were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser markdown-render and layout timings vary, but content size and panel cardinality are fixed and small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: construction is demand-driven, bounded to one small panel, and uses the existing submenu lifecycle and serialization.

Scenarios.Scenario: Activate the HydraFusion Learn more link
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A user gesture invokes IOpenerService.open for the fixed HTTPS URI. Opening the external resource is the requested action; no URL access occurs while merely opening the picker or flyout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open the fixed https://aka.ms/hydrafusion-blog URI through IOpenerService
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one call per explicit Learn more activation
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no HydraFusion Learn more action or opener call from this description.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: On the click action path only; it is off picker and flyout rendering critical paths.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One opener invocation per explicit link activation, independent of model count and picker refresh frequency.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: User-paced activations; the diff adds no automatic retries, Promise fan-out, or burst scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache participates; repeated activations intentionally invoke the opener again.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: renderMarkdown's actionHandler directly calls openerService.open only upon anchor activation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The external handler and eventual navigation latency are environment-dependent, but they are user-requested and not repeated automatically.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the single boundary call is intentional, user-triggered, and neither amplified nor placed on a passive UI path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render HydraFusion descriptions in existing model cards or shared hover consumers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing callers still invoke renderModelDescription/getModelHoverContent during their established render paths. The changed renderer allocates a small return object, and HydraFusion shared hovers append one fixed anchor to markdown already rendered for its tooltip.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most the existing number of rendered model cards/hovers; the new anchor applies only to the singular HydraFusion routing model.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous UI rendering under existing caller ownership; no new asynchronous work or concurrency.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache. Rendered markdown remains owned by the caller's existing DisposableStore.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all repository callers of getModelHoverContent and the changed renderModelDescription call site were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of cards rendered by legacy surfaces varies, but only HydraFusion receives extra DOM and the incremental allocation is constant.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the shared API shape adds only constant, tiny allocations and preserves existing lifecycle ownership.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all eight changed files. The PR adds a single lazy, bounded HydraFusion flyout and a user-triggered opener call; it introduces no realistic hot-path fan-out, concurrency burst, unbounded retention, or material synchronous rendering regression. No findings were submitted.
